edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: older adults after visually significant cataracts
edges.mechanism: Better visual contrast and depth cues after cataract surgery directly improve navigation and hazard detection, making fewer falls plausible.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2023 Pham cohort in Clin Ophthalmol, which ties cataract surgery to falls in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.

evidence.notes: The Association of Cardiovascular and Neurological Comorbidities in Geriatric Patients Sustaining Ocular Trauma.
